Let
\[
z=\frac1\lambda,\qquad q=\frac1\mu .
\]
Since \(0<\lambda<\mu<1\), we have \(z>q>1\). Also
\[
\frac{1-\lambda x}{1-\mu x}
=\frac{\lambda}{\mu}\frac{z-x}{q-x}.
\]
Thus every moment in the modified determinant is multiplied by the common scalar \((\lambda/\mu)^2\) and by the rational factor \(((z-x)/(q-x))^2\). Therefore
\[
\frac{D_n^{\rm rat}(\lambda,\mu)}{D_n}
=
\left(\frac{\lambda}{\mu}\right)^{2n}
\frac{\det\!\left[\int_0^1 x^{i+j}w(x)\left(\frac{z-x}{q-x}\right)^2dx\right]_{i,j=0}^{n-1}}{D_n}.
\]

A standard Christoffel-Geronimus determinant identity gives, for distinct \(z_1,z_2,q_1,q_2>1\),
\[
\frac{D_n\!\left[\prod_{\alpha=1}^2\frac{z_\alpha-x}{q_\alpha-x}w\right]}{D_n[w]}
=
\frac{\det\!\left[F_n(z_\alpha,q_\beta)\right]_{\alpha,\beta=1}^2}
{\det\!\left[(q_\beta-z_\alpha)^{-1}\right]_{\alpha,\beta=1}^2}.
\]
Indeed, the one-point case is
\[
\frac{D_n\!\left[\frac{z-x}{q-x}w\right]}{D_n[w]}
=
R_n(z,q),
\]
and the two-point formula follows by applying the same Christoffel-Geronimus transform twice; the Cauchy denominator accounts for the two external points.

Now let \(z_1,z_2\to z\) and \(q_1,q_2\to q\). Writing \(F=F_n\),
\[
\det[F(z_\alpha,q_\beta)]
\sim
(z_2-z_1)(q_2-q_1)\bigl(F\,F_{zq}-F_zF_q\bigr),
\]
while
\[
\det[(q_\beta-z_\alpha)^{-1}]
\sim
-\frac{(z_2-z_1)(q_2-q_1)}{(q-z)^4}.
\]
Hence the confluent limit is
\[
(q-z)^4\left(F_zF_q-F\,F_{zq}\right)
=
\mathcal G_n(z,q).
\]

Substituting \(z=1/\lambda\) and \(q=1/\mu\), the required ratio is therefore
\[
\boxed{
\frac{D_n^{\mathrm{rat}}(\lambda,\mu)}{D_n}
=
\left(\frac{\lambda}{\mu}\right)^{2n}
\mathcal G_n\!\left(\frac1\lambda,\frac1\mu\right)
}.
\]
